THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.04.2017 PASSED BY THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AT MYSURU, IN MVC NO.730/2014 EXCERSISE BY A SUM OF RS.8,00,000/-.

THESE MFAs, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
UMESH M ADIGA .J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB  MFA No. 7295 of 2017  C/W MFA No. 8267 of 2017  JUDGMENT 1.

Appeals in MFA.No.7295/2017 and MFA No.8267/2017 arise out of the judgment and award passed by the Addl. Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, Mysuru (herein after for short referred as Legal Manager vs Jayaramegowda on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131889078/
3 "Tribunal") in MVC No.730/2014 dated 05.04.2017.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.7295/2017 is filed by the claimant and MFA No.8267/2017 is filed by the insurer.
3. These appeals though slated for hearing on admission, with consent of learned Advocates for both the parties, matters are taken for final disposal.
4. We refer the parties as per their ranks before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.
5. It is the case of the claimant, that on 03.04.2014 in morning 11.30 am, the claimant was going as pillion rider in TVS moped bearing Reg No.KA-45-L-2471.

He met with an accident near Lakshmi Theater, Hunsur - Mysuru Main road; due to rash and negligent driving of canter bearing Reg No.
KA- 09-B-4813, by its driver as a result of which the claimant had sustained grievous injuries.
He had taken treatment in BGS NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB Apollo Hospital, Mysuru and thereafter in Panacea Hospital, J P Nagar, Mysuru.

entities.text: Panacea Hospital, J P Nagar, Mysuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He had taken treatment as an in patient for a period of 1 months.
6. It is further case of claimant that he is an agriculturist and also vegetable vendor and earning was Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been suffering from permanent disability and unable to do any kind of work and lost his earnings.

With these reasons,
prayed to award compensation of Rs. 37,50,000/-.
7. Respondent No.3 - Insurer contended before the tribunal that owner of the vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance.
Therefore, Respondent No.3 has no liability to indemnify the owner of the vehicle.
The petition was bad for non-joinder of necessary parties since the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the TVS Moped by its rider.
Therefore, the claimant is not entitled for compensation.
It also denied all the averments stated in the petition.
With these reasons, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues for consideration.
9. Claimant in order to prove his case, has examined PW. 1 to 3 and got marked documents at EX.P1 to 27.
Respondents have not let in any oral or documentary evidence.

10. The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties and appreciating pleadings and evidence on record,
held that the accident had taken place due to contributory negligence of driver of the canter and rider of TVS Moped; their contribution is in the ratio of 90 : 10.

The Tribunal assessed the age of the claimant as 54 years, his income as Rs.9,000 p.m. and assessed the disability to whole body as 75%
and awarded following compensation.
Sl. No.

Amount in Rs.
 Particulars Legal Manager vs Jayaramegowda on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131889078/
4  1 5,60,000.00  Medical expenses and nourishment  2 Loss of income during laid up period and  65,400.00  rest  Injury pain and sufferings 40,000.00  Loss of future income 8,91,000.00
Future medical expenses 30,000.00
The Tribunal decided the matter by impugned judgment and award dated 05.04.2017.
The Tribunal has also directed respondent Nos.2 and 3 to pay compensation to the extent of 90% since it is found that 10% of contributory negligence was on part of the owner of TVS moped.

The claimant has challenged the impugned judgment both for enhancement of compensation and also fastening entire liability on respondents Nos.2 and 3 and to pay entire amount of compensation because he was pillion rider.
Insurer has also challenged the impugned judgment challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
12. We have heard the arguments of learned Advocates for both sides.
13. Learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the owner, rider and insurer of TVS Moped bearing No.KA-45-L- 2471 are not parties to the present proceedings.

In the absence of the owner and the insurer of the said moped, the Tribunal has assessed the negligence of rider of the moped,
which is contrary to the Settled principles of law.
He further submits that Tribunal has not considered the income of NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB claimant properly and assessment of the disability is also not in accordance with evidence of PWs.2 and 3.
He further submits that amount of compensation awarded under other heads are also meager and therefore prays to enhance compensation.
14. The learned Advocate for insurer submits that negligence fastened on the rider of moped is very less and in fact rider of moped himself was responsible for the accident.
The Tribunal has not considered evidence properly while awarding compensation and awarded excess amount of compensation.
Hence, prayed to recalculate the same.

15. The Tribunal while considering issue No.1, at para Nos.8 and 9 assessed the evidence on record and came to conclusion that the accident had taken place due to contributory negligence of driver of Legal Manager vs Jayaramegowda on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131889078/
5
the canter as well as rider of the two wheeler and their contribution was in the ratio of 90 : 10.
The said finding is on the basis of the materials available on record and it does not call for any interference by this Court.
16. It is not in dispute that claimant has sustained injuries in vehicle accident.

According to PW.2 Dr. Goutham Gugati, claimant had sustained head injury and underwent NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB brain surgery of right fronto temporal - parietal craniotomy and evacuation of acute SDH and left fronto temporal parietal craniotomy and removal of contusion and evacuation of Hematoma on 03.04.2014.
He has also taken continuous treatment in said hospital.

PW.2 has examined him on 04.07.2016 and opined that claimant was conscious, but not oriented and was walking with support;
he had severe dementia, emotional liability and irrelevant speech.

PW.2 has also consulted clinical psychologist and both of them opined that claimant is suffering from permanent disability to whole body to the extent of 90%.
17.
PW.2 has also stated in his evidence that claimant needs continuous medication and approximately Rs.5,000/- p.m. is required to the same.
Similarly PW.3 - Orthopedic Surgeon assessed the total disability to the extent of 32.37% to right lower limb.
In the cross-examination of both PWs.2 and 3 they have supported their evidence.
Considering the age of the claimant as well as injuries sustained by him in the accident, permanent disability assessed by the Tribunal is on lower side.
According to the submissions of learned advocate for the appellant / claimant, the claimant is bed ridden and unable to - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB do any activities.

Considering all these submissions and evidence available on record the disability of claimant affecting his earning capacity to the whole body, is taken at 85%.
18.

Admittedly, the claimant has not led legal evidence to prove that he was earning Rs.9,000/- p.m.
or Rs.15,000/- p.m., as contended.
The Tribunal assessed his notional income as Rs.9,000/- p.m.

While settlement of Motor Vehicle compensation claim petition before the Lok Adalath, in respect of accidents that occurred during the year 2014, the notional income of a victim of an accident is considered as Rs.8,500/- p.m.
Since the accident in question occurred in the year 2014, the same could be applied to the present case.
It is not in dispute that the multiplier applicable in the present case is '11'.
On the basis of the said factors, loss of future earnings due to permanent disability is assessed.
19. Looking to the evidence of PWs.2 and 3 and also material evidence placed on record, the claimant is bed ridden from the date of accident and was unable to do any kind of work.

Hence,
some amount of compensation to be awarded towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

The - 11 - Legal Manager vs Jayaramegowda on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131889078/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'pain and sufferings' and 'future medical expenses' are on lower side.
Tribunal has awarded compensation towards 'medical expenses' keeping in view the material available on record and it does not call for any interference.
20. The Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards 'loss of amenities'.
Learned Advocate for claimant submits that petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability; for daily pursuits he has to depend on others.
Someone has to attend him around the clock; considering injuries and disability, said submission is acceptable.
The claimant has lost lot of amenities available to healthy person which needs to be compensated.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, following amount of compensation is awarded.

Sl. Particulars Amount (Rs.)
 No.
 1 Loss of future earnings 9,53,700  (8,500/- x 12 x 11 x 85%)
 2 Loss of income during laid up 51,000  period  3 Pain and sufferings 1,00,000  4
Medical expenses 5,60,000
5 Future Medical expenses 50,000  6 Loss of amenities 1,00,000  TOTAL 18,14,700  - 12 -  NC:
KHC:33364-DB

Claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,28,300/-.
21.
Admittedly, the claimant was pillion rider and accident had not taken place due to his negligence.
Therefore, the deduction of 10% from compensation amount awarded is erroneous.
The claimant can claim the compensation from either of joint-tortfeasors since the owner and insurer of the two wheeler - TVS moped, are not parties to the present case.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are owner and insurer of the lorry.
Hence Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are liable to pay the entire amount of compensation.
22. The learned Advocate for insurer seriously objects for awarding interest at 9% p.a on the amount of compensation.

The rate of interest awarded by the bank on FD A/c for a period of one year is 6%
p.a.
Same may please be awarded.
The learned Advocate for appellant / claimant submits that the Tribunal exercised its discretion and awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a and same shall be maintained.

Legal Manager vs Jayaramegowda on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131889078/
7 23.
Considering the submission made by both the parties before the Tribunal, the Tribunal had awarded interest at the rate of 9%.
At present, the rate of interest on FD for a period - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB of one year is around 6% p.a.
Therefore, to that extent the rate of interest can be reduced from 9% p.a. to 6% p.a, from the date of petition till payment of the enhanced amount of compensation.

24. From the aforesaid discussion, we pass the following :
ORDER i) MFA. No.7295/2017 and MFA. No.8267/2017 are disposed of.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 05.04.2017, passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.730/2014 is modified as under:
The claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.18,14,700/- as against Rs.15,86,400/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,28,300/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
iii) Respondent No.3 shall deposit the said amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

Release and deposit of amount are as ordered by the Tribunal.
v) The amount deposited by the insurer in MFA. No.8267/2017 shall be transmitted to the Tribunal to release the said amount to the claimant in terms of judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Sd/-

Claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,28,300/-.
21.
Therefore, the deduction of 10% from compensation amount awarded is erroneous.
The claimant can claim the compensation from either of joint-tortfeasors since the owner and insurer of the two wheeler - TVS moped, are not parties to the present case.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are owner and insurer of the lorry.
Hence Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are liable to pay the entire amount of compensation.
22. The learned Advocate for insurer seriously objects for awarding interest at 9% p.a on the amount of compensation.

The rate of interest awarded by the bank on FD A/c for a period of one year is 6%
p.a.
The learned Advocate for appellant / claimant submits that the Tribunal exercised its discretion and awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a and same shall be maintained.
Considering the submission made by both the parties before the Tribunal, the Tribunal had awarded interest at the rate of 9%.
At present, the rate of interest on FD for a period - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33364-DB of one year is around 6% p.a.
Therefore, to that extent the rate of interest can be reduced from 9% p.a. to 6% p.a, from the date of petition till payment of the enhanced amount of compensation.

24. From the aforesaid discussion, we pass the following :
ORDER i) MFA. No.7295/2017 and MFA. No.8267/2017 are disposed of.
ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 05.04.2017, passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.730/2014 is modified as under:
The claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.18,14,700/- as against Rs.15,86,400/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,28,300/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
iii) Respondent No.3 shall deposit the said amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
